q: In a Rajbhasha quiz, an employee is asked about the Dakshin Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha, founded by Mahatma Gandhi for the propagation of Hindi in South India. It was founded in the year 1918 at:

options.C: Hyderabad
options.D: Kochi

e: The Dakshin Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha, founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1918 for propagating Hindi in South India, was set up at Madras.

q: An employee compiling Census language figures for a Rajbhasha note is asked what proportion of the population of India returned Hindi as their mother tongue in the Census of India, 2011. The correct figure is approximately:

options.C: About 43.6 per cent
options.D: About 58 per cent

e: In Census 2011, about 43.6 per cent of India's population returned Hindi as their mother tongue, making it by far the largest mother tongue.

q: An employee compiling Census language figures for a Rajbhasha note is asked to name, as per the Census of India, 2011, the second most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India. The correct answer is:

options.C: Tamil
options.D: Bengali

e: Bengali is the second most widely spoken mother tongue in India as per Census 2011, after Hindi.

q: A school student sponsored for a Hindi programme asks who invented the Ol Chiki script, used for writing the Santhali language, and in which year. The correct answer is:

options.A: Pandit Raghunath Murmu, in the year 1925
options.C: Jaipal Singh Munda, in the year 1947
options.D: Shibu Soren, in the year 1972

e: The Ol Chiki script for Santhali was invented by Pandit Raghunath Murmu in 1925; Santhali written in Ol Chiki later entered the Eighth Schedule.

q: A Rajbhasha note on Indian scripts records the number of scripts in which the Konkani language is written. The correct number is:

options.C: Three scripts
options.D: Seven scripts

e: Konkani is written in five scripts: Devanagari, Roman, Kannada, Malayalam and Perso-Arabic, though Devanagari is its official script in Goa.

q: A member of a study circle asks on what condition the use of the English language for the transaction of business in Parliament was to continue after fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution. Under Article 120(2) of the Constitution, such use was to discontinue after that period, unless:

options.A: The President by order otherwise provides
options.C: Parliament by law otherwise provides
options.D: The Official Language Commission recommends otherwise

e: Article 120(2) provided that English would discontinue for business in Parliament after fifteen years unless Parliament by law otherwise provided, which it did through the Official Languages Act.

q: A constitutional note records the special provision in Article 210(2) of the Constitution for the Legislatures of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, for which the period of fifteen years for the continued use of English in the State Legislature was substituted by a period of:

options.C: Thirty years
options.D: Twenty-five years

e: The proviso to Article 210(2) substitutes twenty-five years for fifteen years in relation to the Legislatures of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh for continued use of English.

q: A Central Government office has to send a communication to a member of the public residing in Region 'A'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a communication sent to a person in Region 'A' shall be in:

options.C: The regional language of the region
options.D: Hindi or English, at the choice of the officer issuing it

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications from a Central Government office to a person in Region A shall be in Hindi.

q: A litigant asks in which language the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Maharashtra conduct their work. The correct answer is:

options.C: English
options.D: Gujarati

e: The subordinate or district courts in Maharashtra conduct their work in Marathi, the official language of the State.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Public Account". The correct equivalent is:

options.C: Lok Lekha
options.D: Khata Bahi

e: The Public Account, into which public money held in trust is credited under Article 266, is rendered as Lok Lekha.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Appropriation". The correct equivalent is:

options.C: Niyojan
options.D: Viniyog

e: Appropriation, the authorisation to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund for specified purposes, is rendered as Viniyog.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Vote on Account". The correct equivalent is:

options.C: Viniyog
options.D: Anudan

e: Vote on Account, the advance grant taken pending full approval of the budget, is rendered as Lekhanudan.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Balance Sheet". The correct equivalent is:

options.C: Aay-Vyay Vivaran
options.D: Sthiti Vivaran

e: The Balance Sheet, showing the financial position with assets and liabilities, is rendered as Tulan Patra.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bodo language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, is written in the Devanagari script.
2. In the State of Goa, Konkani, the official language of the State, is used in the Devanagari script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: Bodo, an Eighth Schedule language, is written in the Devanagari script, and Konkani, the official language of Goa, is used there in Devanagari.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Urdu language is written from right to left.
2. The United Nations has six official languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Urdu is written from right to left in the Perso-Arabic script, and the United Nations has six official languages.

q: In a Rajbhasha quiz, an employee is asked in which year Sanskrit was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India. The correct answer is:
e: Sanskrit was accorded classical language status in 2005, a year after Tamil became the first such language.

q: In a Rajbhasha quiz, an employee is asked in which year Telugu was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India. The correct answer is:
e: Telugu was accorded classical language status in 2008, along with Kannada, on satisfying the criteria laid down for classical languages.

q: A Rajbhasha note on the official languages of the States has to record the official language of the State of Assam. The correct entry is:

options.C: Hindi
options.D: Bodo

e: Assamese is the official language of Assam, used for the official purposes of the State.

q: A tourist information note has to record the official languages of the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The correct entry is:

options.C: Hindi and English
options.D: Hindi and Bengali

e: Hindi and English are the official languages of the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

q: A Rajbhasha note records that Bengali is used as an official language in the Barak Valley region of a State. That State is:

options.C: Bihar
options.D: Assam

e: Bengali is used as an additional official language in the Barak Valley region of Assam, where Bengali speakers form a large part of the population.

q: A member of a study circle asks what the President could authorise by order during the first fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution in the matter of language. Under Article 343(2) of the Constitution, during that period the President could authorise:

options.A: The use of the Hindi language in addition to the English language for any of the official purposes of the Union
options.B: The discontinuance of the English language for all official purposes of the Union
options.C: The use of any language mentioned in the Eighth Schedule in the proceedings of Parliament
options.D: The use of the Devanagari form of numerals in the accounts of the States

e: Article 343(2) empowered the President, during the first fifteen years, to authorise by order the use of Hindi in addition to English for any official purposes of the Union.

q: The head of a newly opened Central Government office in a southern State contends that the Official Languages Act, 1963 does not extend to his State. The correct position is that the Act extends to:

options.C: The Hindi-speaking States only
options.D: All States except Tamil Nadu

e: The Official Languages Act, 1963 extends to the whole of India; no State, including a southern State, is outside its application.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Draft". The correct equivalent is:

options.C: Suchna
options.D: Praroop

e: The standard equivalent of Draft, meaning a preliminary text prepared for approval, is Praroop.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Endorsement". The correct equivalent is:

options.C: Prishthankan
options.D: Pramanikaran

e: Endorsement, the writing made on the back of a document, is rendered as Prishthankan, from Prishtha meaning the back or page.

q: A Central Government office issues a notice inviting applications from the public in English only, contending that a public notice is not a document covered by the language law. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct, notices being outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.B: The contention is correct if the notice is issued from an office located in Region 'B'
options.C: The contention is correct if a Hindi version is pasted on the notice board of the office
options.D: The contention is not correct; a notice issued by a Central Government office is required to be issued in both Hindi and English under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963

e: Notices are among the documents covered by Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, so a public notice of a Central Government office must be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'B' issued 450 letters during a quarter, of which 360 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 75 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B' being 90 per cent
options.C: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 55 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'B'

e: 360 of 450 letters is 80 per cent, which falls short of the Annual Programme target of 90 per cent for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region B.

q: A Central Government office is located at Bhopal in the State of Madhya Pradesh. During a quarter it issued 350 letters, all of which were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for its region being 100 per cent
options.B: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for its region being 90 per cent
options.C: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in its region being 100 per cent
options.D: No target applies to the office, its State being outside all regions

e: Bhopal is in Madhya Pradesh, a Region A State where the target for correspondence originating in Hindi is 100 per cent, and all 350 letters in Hindi just meet that target.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'C' issued 700 letters during a quarter, of which 350 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' being 55 per cent
options.B: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 55 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 40 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'C'

e: 350 of 700 letters is 50 per cent, which falls short of the Annual Programme target of 55 per cent for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region C.

q: During a quarter, a Central Government office recorded 90 notes on files, of which 30 were written in Hindi. With reference to the target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target being 30 per cent
options.B: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target being 30 per cent
options.C: No target is fixed for noting on files in Hindi
options.D: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for noting on files in Hindi being 30 per cent

e: 30 of 90 notes is about 33 per cent, which exceeds the target of 30 per cent fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi.

q: An accounts clerk passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 64 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:
e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme cash award slabs for Pragya, 64 per cent marks fall in the slab carrying an award of Rs 1,600.

q: A junior accounts assistant passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 71 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.D: No cash award, the minimum marks required being 75 per cent

e: Under the Pragya cash award slabs, 71 per cent marks fall in the higher slab carrying an award of Rs 2,400.

q: A typist in a Central Government office passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 94 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 98 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold of 90 per cent or more marks for the typewriting examination having been secured
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Pragya examination in the same year
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months instead

e: A cash award in the Hindi typewriting examination is admissible on securing 90 per cent or more marks, and 94 per cent satisfies that threshold.

q: A stenographer passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 90 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 98 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if his stenography speed exceeds 100 words per minute
options.C: He becomes entitled to a lumpsum award in lieu of the cash award
options.D: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold of 88 per cent or more marks for the stenography examination having been secured

e: A cash award in the Hindi stenography examination is admissible on securing 88 per cent or more marks, and 90 per cent satisfies that threshold.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 26 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 25 words per minute
options.B: He does not pass on speed, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination being 30 words per minute
options.C: He passes, the examination being decided on marks alone and not on speed
options.D: He passes only if he secures 90 per cent marks in the Pragya examination

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination is 30 words per minute, so a speed of 26 words per minute does not qualify.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 90 words per minute. As regards the prescribed speed standard, the correct position is:

options.A: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.B: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 120 words per minute
options.C: He meets the prescribed speed standard only if he also attains 30 words per minute in Hindi typewriting
options.D: He meets the prescribed speed standard, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination being 80 words per minute

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination is 80 words per minute, so 90 words per minute meets the standard.

q: A 44-year-old employee, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years
options.B: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 40 years
options.C: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: He must undergo the training on payment of the prescribed fee

e: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for a Central Government employee who lacks working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained 45 years of age, so a 44-year-old must undergo it.

q: An employee aged 48 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is proposed to be nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for all employees irrespective of age
options.B: He is exempt only if he has attained the age of 58 years
options.C: The training is not compulsory for him, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years
options.D: He must undergo the training on payment of the prescribed fee

e: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years, so a 48-year-old without working knowledge of Hindi is not bound to undergo it.

q: A Central Government office has a total staff strength of 300, of whom 258 have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, notification requiring 90 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office can be notified, 80 per cent or more of its staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.C: The office can be notified only if all its staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: Individual offices cannot be notified under the Official Language Rules, 1976

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi; 258 of 300 is 86 per cent, so the office can be notified.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 10,500 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible, eligibility requiring noting and drafting of at least 20,000 words in Hindi in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration only if he has done noting and drafting of at least 50,000 words in Hindi in a year
options.C: He is eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being noting and drafting of at least 10,000 words in Hindi in a year
options.D: No cash award scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi exists

e: The incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi requires at least 10,000 words in a year; 10,500 words make the employee eligible for consideration.

q: Eleven months have passed since an employee was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination, and he asks whether that personal pay will still be admissible to him in the current month. The correct position is:

options.A: The personal pay stood discontinued after three months from the grant
options.B: The personal pay stood discontinued after six months from the grant
options.C: The personal pay stands converted into a lumpsum award in the eleventh month
options.D: The personal pay continues to be admissible, personal pay equal to one increment being admissible for a period of 12 months

e: Personal pay equal to one increment granted on passing the prescribed Hindi examination is admissible for 12 months, so it continues in the eleventh month.

q: A Central Government office frames certain rules and issues them in Hindi only, contending that issue in the Official Language of the Union alone is sufficient. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is:

options.C: Both Hindi and English
options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

e: Rules framed by a Central Government office are documents under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 and must be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: A Central Government office has to send a communication to a State Government office located in Region 'B'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication shall ordinarily be in:

options.C: The regional language of the State
options.D: Either Hindi or the regional language, at the writer's choice

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications to a State Government office in Region B shall ordinarily be in Hindi, as Region B communication is also prescribed in Hindi.

q: An officer of one Ministry of the Central Government has to write to another Ministry of the Central Government on an official matter. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication may be in:

options.C: The regional language of the State where the Ministry is located
options.D: Hindi or English

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between Ministries or Departments of the Central Government may be either in Hindi or in English.

q: Two Central Government offices, both situated in Region 'A' and neither of them being a Ministry or Department or its attached or subordinate office, have to correspond with each other. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, such communications shall be in:

options.C: The regional language of the State
options.D: Hindi or the regional language, at the writer's choice

e: Under Rule 3 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between Central Government offices situated in Region A, other than Ministries and their offices, shall be in Hindi.

q: A member of the public wishes to submit an application to a Central Government office in connection with an official matter. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, he may submit the application in:

options.C: English only
options.D: The official language of the State only

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a member of the public may submit an application or representation to a Central Government office in Hindi or in English.

q: An employee of a Central Government office, who possesses working knowledge of Hindi, records his noting on a file in English, although he could have recorded it in Hindi. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The noting is irregular, an employee possessing working knowledge of Hindi being required to note in Hindi only
options.B: The noting must be rewritten in Hindi by the Hindi Translator of the office
options.C: The noting can be recorded only in the regional language of the State
options.D: The noting is in order, an employee who possesses working knowledge of Hindi being free to make noting and drafting in Hindi or in English, as he may choose

e: The Official Language Rules, 1976 leave an employee possessing working knowledge of Hindi free to make noting and drafting in Hindi or in English as he chooses; noting in English is in order.

q: An office of a public sector undertaking, owned and controlled by the Central Government, asks whether the Official Language Rules, 1976 apply to it as a Central Government office. The correct position is:

options.A: The office is included in the expression "Central Government office" for the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, being an office of a company or corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government
options.B: The office is not covered, only the offices of Ministries and Departments of the Central Government being covered
options.C: The office is covered only if it is located in Region 'A'
options.D: The office is covered only during Hindi Pakhwada

e: The definition of Central Government office in the Official Language Rules, 1976 includes an office of a company or corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government, so the rules apply.

q: The Legislature of a State has not, by law, adopted any language as the official language of the State. Under the proviso to Article 345 of the Constitution, the language that continues to be used for those official purposes of the State for which it was being used immediately before the commencement of the Constitution is:

options.C: The language of the largest linguistic minority of the State
options.D: Sanskrit

e: Under the proviso to Article 345, until the State Legislature adopts another language by law, English continues for those official purposes of the State for which it was used before the Constitution.

q: Two States agree between themselves that a particular language shall be the official language for communication between them. Under the proviso to Article 346 of the Constitution, the language so agreed upon is:

options.B: The regional language of either State
options.C: Hindi
options.D: Sanskrit

e: The proviso to Article 346 provides that where two or more States agree that Hindi shall be the official language for communication between them, Hindi shall be so used.

q: In a State, it is proposed that Hindi should be used, in addition to English, for the judgments, decrees and orders of the High Court of that State. Under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, such use may be authorised by:

options.A: The Chief Justice of the High Court on his own
options.B: The Union Minister of Law and Justice
options.C: The Bar Council of the State
options.D: The Governor of the State, with the previous consent of the President

e: Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 permits use of Hindi, in addition to English, for High Court judgments, decrees and orders when authorised by the Governor with the President's previous consent.

q: A note on linguistic minorities has to record the place where the headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities, appointed under Article 350B of the Constitution, is located. The correct entry is:

options.C: Lucknow
options.D: Bhopal

e: The headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities, the Special Officer under Article 350B, is located at Prayagraj (Allahabad).

q: An officer preparing a brief on the safeguards for linguistic minorities asks to whom the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed under Article 350B of the Constitution, submits his reports on the working of those safeguards. The correct answer is:

options.C: To the Union Home Minister
options.D: To the Governor of the State concerned

e: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities submits his reports on the working of the safeguards for linguistic minorities to the President, who causes them to be laid before Parliament.

q: An employee preparing a note on the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution lists English among the languages included in that Schedule. The correct position is:

options.A: The list is correct, English being included in the Eighth Schedule
options.B: English is NOT included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution
options.C: English was included in the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003
options.D: English was included in the Eighth Schedule at the commencement of the Constitution

e: English is not among the 22 languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, though it continues in official use under other provisions and law.

q: A Rajbhasha quiz asks which set of languages was added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003. The correct answer is:

options.C: English, Bodo and Dogri
options.D: Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali

e: The Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule, raising the total to 22 languages.

q: A Rajbhasha note on the official languages of the States has to record the official language of the State of Odisha. The correct entry is:

options.C: Telugu
options.D: Hindi

e: Odia is the official language of Odisha, the first State formed on a linguistic basis in 1936.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar and the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language are presented every year on the occasion of Hindi Diwas (14th September).
2. The award of the Department of Official Language for excellence in the implementation of the Official Language Policy, now known as the Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar, was earlier known as the Indira Gandhi Rajbhasha Puraskar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Rajbhasha Kirti and Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskars are presented on Hindi Diwas, 14 September, and the Kirti Puraskar was earlier called the Indira Gandhi Rajbhasha Puraskar.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Parangat course, meant for employees who have passed Pragya and require advanced proficiency in Hindi, is conducted through correspondence by the Central Hindi Directorate.
2. In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the Prabodh course is intended for employees who do not possess any knowledge of Hindi, i.e., beginners.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Parangat, the advanced course after Pragya, is run through correspondence by the Central Hindi Directorate, and Prabodh is the beginners course for those with no knowledge of Hindi.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Commission to be constituted under Article 344 of the Constitution consists of a Chairman and other members representing the different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule.
2. Under Article 344 of the Constitution, it is the duty of the Official Language Commission to make recommendations to the President as to the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union and the restrictions on the use of the English language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Article 344 Commission consists of a Chairman and members representing the Eighth Schedule languages, and it recommends on progressive use of Hindi and restrictions on English.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 347 of the Constitution, if the President is satisfied that a substantial proportion of the population of a State desires the use of a language spoken by them to be recognised by the State, he may direct that such language shall also be officially recognised throughout that State or any part thereof for specified purposes.
2. Under the proviso to Article 346 of the Constitution, where two or more States agree that Hindi shall be the official language for communication between such States, such provision shall apply to the communication between those States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.C: 2 only
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: Article 347 empowers the President to direct official recognition of a language desired by a substantial proportion of a State's population, and the Article 346 proviso covers inter-State Hindi by agreement.

q: An officer revising the award entries in the Rajbhasha file of his office has to strike out the one entry that is not correct. Which one of the following entries relating to the Rajbhasha awards of the Department of Official Language and of Indian Railways is the incorrect one?

options.A: The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.B: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar is awarded to Ministries/Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy
options.C: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar is awarded for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects
options.D: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar is awarded to Ministries/Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy

e: Entry D is incorrect because the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar is for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects, not for Ministries, undertakings and banks; that implementation award is the Kirti Puraskar.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Memorandum". The correct equivalent is:

options.C: Gyapan
options.D: Paripatra

e: The standard equivalent of Memorandum, an official communication within offices, is Gyapan.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Reminder". The correct equivalent is:

options.C: Praptipatra
options.D: Anusmarak

e: The standard equivalent of Reminder, sent to recall an earlier reference, is Anusmarak.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Notification". The correct equivalent is:

options.C: Swikriti
options.D: Karyavritt

e: The standard equivalent of Notification, a matter published in the Gazette, is Adhisuchna.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Sanction" (of expenditure). The correct equivalent is:

options.C: Swikriti
options.D: Aagya

e: Sanction of expenditure, meaning formal approval or acceptance, is rendered as Swikriti in the standard administrative glossary.

q: An Adarsh (model) station of a Zonal Railway, adjudged excellent in the implementation of the Official Language Policy, claims the Rajbhasha recognition admissible on Indian Railways for such performance. The correct position is:

options.A: Shields and cash awards for excellence in the implementation of the Official Language Policy are given on Indian Railways, besides Zonal Railways and Divisions, also to Adarsh stations and Adarsh workshops
options.B: Such recognition is admissible only to Zonal Railways, and not to stations
options.C: Such recognition is admissible only to Divisions, and not to stations
options.D: Such recognition is admissible only to retired railway employees

e: On Indian Railways, shields and cash awards for excellence in Official Language implementation are given, besides Zonal Railways and Divisions, also to Adarsh stations and Adarsh workshops.

q: A Rajbhasha note on railway institutions has to record the name of the first Chairman of the Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti. The correct entry is:

options.C: B. G. Kher
options.D: G. B. Pant

e: Lalit Narayan Mishra, the then Railway Minister, was the first Chairman of the Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti, the advisory committee for Hindi in Railways.

q: The Legislature of a State has prescribed a language other than English for use in the Acts passed by it, and an English translation of such an Act is published under the authority of the Governor in the Official Gazette of the State. Under Article 348(3) of the Constitution, that translation shall be deemed to be:

options.A: A mere unofficial summary of the Act
options.C: The authoritative text thereof in the English language
options.D: A draft requiring the approval of Parliament

e: Under Article 348(3), an English translation of a State Act published under the Governor's authority in the State Gazette is deemed the authoritative text of the Act in English.

q: A State Legislature passes an Act in the State language, and its Hindi translation is published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the Governor of the State. An officer to whom that translation is placed for reference asks about its legal status. Under Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, that translation shall be deemed to be:

options.A: A document of no legal value
options.B: Valid only in the States of Region 'A'
options.C: The authoritative text thereof in Hindi
options.D: Effective only after approval by the State Legislature

e: Under Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a Hindi translation of a State Act published under the Governor's authority in the State Gazette is deemed the authoritative text in Hindi.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The websites of Central Government offices are required to be maintained in Hindi and English, i.e., in bilingual form.
2. Software packages procured for use in Central Government offices are required to have the facility of working in Hindi as well, i.e., bilingual (Hindi-English) capability.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: Central Government office websites must be bilingual in Hindi and English, and software procured for such offices must have bilingual Hindi-English working capability.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The training imparted to Central Government employees under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is free of cost during office hours, the training period being treated as on duty.
2. The Hindi Teaching Scheme for Central Government employees is administered by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Hindi Teaching Scheme training is free, held during office hours and treated as on duty, and the scheme is administered by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'A' issued 250 letters during a quarter, of which 230 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'A' being 90 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'A' being 100 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'A' being 75 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'A'

e: 230 of 250 letters is 92 per cent, which falls short of the 100 per cent target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region A.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'C' issued 900 letters during a quarter, of which 540 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' being 55 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 75 per cent
options.C: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 60 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'C'

e: 540 of 900 letters is 60 per cent, which exceeds the 55 per cent target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region C.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'B' issued 550 letters during a quarter, of which 440 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 80 per cent
options.B: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 55 per cent
options.C: The office has met the target, no percentage being prescribed for Region 'B'
options.D: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B' being 90 per cent

e: 440 of 550 letters is 80 per cent, which falls short of the 90 per cent target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region B.

q: During a quarter, a Central Government office recorded 140 notes on files, of which 49 were written in Hindi. With reference to the target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target being 50 per cent
options.B: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target being 35 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for noting on files in Hindi being 30 per cent
options.D: No target is fixed for noting on files in Hindi

e: 49 of 140 notes is 35 per cent, which exceeds the 30 per cent target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi.

q: For its Quarterly Progress Report, an office counts its Hindi correspondence. During the quarter it issued 130 letters, of which 51 were originally written in Hindi and 79 were English drafts translated into Hindi before issue. The number to be counted as Hindi correspondence is:
e: Only letters originally written in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence; English drafts translated into Hindi do not, so the count is 51 and not 130.

q: A clerk in a divisional accounts office passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 75 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.D: No cash award, the minimum marks required being 80 per cent

e: Under the Pragya cash award slabs, 75 per cent marks fall in the top slab carrying an award of Rs 2,400.

q: A senior accounts assistant passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 77 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:
e: Under the Pragya cash award slabs, 77 per cent marks fall in the top slab carrying an award of Rs 2,400.

q: A typist in a Central Government office passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 86 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 90 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 85 per cent marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Pragya examination in the same year
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 12 months instead

e: No cash award is admissible in the Hindi typewriting examination at 86 per cent, because the prescribed threshold is 90 per cent or more marks.

q: A stenographer passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 96 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 98 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold of 88 per cent or more marks for the stenography examination having been secured
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if his stenography speed exceeds 100 words per minute
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 12 months instead

e: A cash award in the Hindi stenography examination is admissible on securing 88 per cent or more marks, and 96 per cent comfortably satisfies that threshold.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 36 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He passes on speed, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination being 30 words per minute
options.B: He does not pass on speed, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 35 words per minute
options.C: He does not pass, the examination being decided on marks alone and not on speed
options.D: He passes only if he secures 90 per cent marks in the Pragya examination

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination is 30 words per minute, so 36 words per minute qualifies on speed.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 78 words per minute. As regards the prescribed speed standard, the correct position is:

options.A: He meets the prescribed speed standard, the prescribed speed being 70 words per minute
options.B: He meets the prescribed speed standard only if he also attains 30 words per minute in Hindi typewriting
options.C: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 120 words per minute
options.D: He falls short, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination being 80 words per minute

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination is 80 words per minute, so 78 words per minute falls short of the standard.

q: A 33-year-old employee, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 40 years
options.B: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years
options.C: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: He must undergo the training only after attaining the age of 45 years

e: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for an employee without working knowledge of Hindi who has not attained 45 years, so a 33-year-old must undergo the training.

q: An employee aged 51 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is proposed to be nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for him irrespective of his age
options.B: He must undergo the training only if his office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976
options.C: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for him, he having attained the age of 45 years
options.D: He must undergo the training only if he is posted in Region 'C'

e: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years, so a 51-year-old is not bound to undergo it.

q: A Central Government office has a total staff strength of 400, of whom 368 have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 90 per cent or more
options.C: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 85 per cent or more
options.D: Notification is not permissible for offices located in Region 'B'

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 per cent or more of the staff to have working knowledge of Hindi; 368 of 400 is 92 per cent, so the office can be notified.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 13,500 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 20,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration only if the noting was done in an office notified under Rule 10(4)
options.C: He is not eligible for consideration, the scheme applying only to noting done in Region 'A' offices
options.D: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year

e: The incentive scheme requires at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year; 13,500 words make the employee eligible for consideration for the cash award.

q: An accounts officer preparing a note on Article 343 of the Constitution records the matter for which Parliament may by law provide, for the purposes specified in that Article. The correct entry is that Parliament may so provide for the use of:

options.A: Roman numerals for all official purposes of the Union
options.B: The numerals of the regional languages for the accounts of the Union
options.C: The Persian form of numerals for correspondence with the States
options.D: The Devanagari form of numerals

e: Article 343 provides that the form of numerals for official purposes of the Union shall be the international form of Indian numerals, but Parliament may by law provide for the Devanagari form of numerals.

q: The period of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution has expired, and an officer asks whether English may continue to be used, in addition to Hindi, for the official purposes of the Union. Under Section 3(1) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is:

options.A: English cannot be used for any official purpose after the expiry of that period
options.B: English may be used only for correspondence with foreign Governments
options.C: English may continue to be used, in addition to Hindi, for all the official purposes of the Union and for the transaction of business in Parliament
options.D: English may be used only in the proceedings of the Supreme Court and the High Courts

e: Section 3(1) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides that English shall continue to be used, in addition to Hindi, for all official purposes of the Union and for business in Parliament even after fifteen years.

q: A Central Government office frames certain bye-laws and issues them in English only, contending that bye-laws are internal documents outside the language law. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is:

options.C: The regional language of the State where the office is located
options.D: Both Hindi and English

e: Bye-laws are among the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, so they must be issued in both Hindi and English, not in English only.

q: A Central Government office has to send a communication to a State Government office located in Region 'C'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication shall be issued in:

options.C: The regional language of the State
options.D: Hindi accompanied by an English translation

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications from a Central Government office to a State Government office in Region C shall be in English.

q: A Central Government office has to send a communication to a State Government office located in Region 'A'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication shall be in:

options.B: The regional language of the State
options.C: Hindi
options.D: Hindi and English, in duplicate

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications from a Central Government office to a State Government office in Region A shall be in Hindi.

q: In a State, it is proposed that Hindi should be used in the proceedings of the High Court of that State. Under Article 348(2) of the Constitution, such use may be authorised by:

options.A: The Chief Justice of the High Court on his own
options.B: The Governor of the State, with the previous consent of the President
options.C: The State Legislature by a simple resolution
options.D: The President, without reference to the State

e: Article 348(2) empowers the Governor, with the previous consent of the President, to authorise the use of Hindi in the proceedings of the State's High Court.

q: An officer preparing a brief on the safeguards for linguistic minorities asks what the duty of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed under Article 350B of the Constitution, is. The correct answer is:

options.A: To promote the use of Hindi in the minority areas
options.B: To conduct the decennial census in minority areas
options.C: To inspect Hindi training centres in the States
options.D: To investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution

e: Under Article 350B, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities must investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution.

q: An officer drafting a note on the development of Hindi under Article 351 of the Constitution records the source from which Hindi shall draw for its vocabulary, in enriching itself by assimilating the forms, style and expressions of Hindustani and the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule. The correct entry is:

options.A: Primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages
options.C: Mainly from Persian and Urdu
options.D: Only from the regional languages

e: Article 351 directs that Hindi shall draw, for its vocabulary, primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages, while assimilating forms and expressions of Hindustani and Eighth Schedule languages.

q: A member of the Legislature of a State is unable to express himself adequately in the official language of the State, in Hindi or in English, and wishes to address the House in his mother tongue. Under Article 210 of the Constitution, he may do so:

options.A: Only through an interpreter arranged by the State Government
options.C: With the permission of the presiding officer of the House
options.D: Only if the Governor permits it in writing in advance

e: Under Article 210, a member of a State Legislature who cannot adequately express himself in the State's official language, Hindi or English may, with the presiding officer's permission, address the House in his mother tongue.

q: A newly posted section officer asks by whom the rules for carrying out the purposes of the Official Languages Act, 1963 are made. Under Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the power to make such rules vests in:

options.A: The Parliamentary Committee on Official Language
options.C: The State Governments
options.D: The Department of Official Language acting alone

e: Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

q: A Rajbhasha note on the history of Hindi training records the instrument by which in-service Hindi training was made compulsory for Central Government employees. That instrument was:

options.C: A resolution of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti
options.D: The Presidential Order of 1960

e: In-service Hindi training for Central Government employees was made compulsory under the Presidential Order of 1960, issued on the recommendations on the Official Language Commission and the parliamentary committee.

q: A dealing assistant asks what the main function of the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology (CSTT) is. The correct answer is:

options.A: To evolve and define scientific and technical terms in Hindi and other Indian languages and to publish glossaries and definitional dictionaries
options.B: To conduct Hindi examinations for Central Government employees
options.C: To inspect Central Government offices for use of Hindi
options.D: To translate judgments of the Supreme Court and High Courts

e: The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology evolves and defines scientific and technical terms in Hindi and other Indian languages and publishes glossaries and definitional dictionaries.

q: A section officer asks which office prepares the Hindi translation of Bills introduced in Parliament and of Central Acts. The correct answer is:

options.C: The Official Language Wing (Rajbhasha Khand) of the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice
options.D: The Lok Sabha Secretariat

e: The Hindi translation of Bills introduced in Parliament and of Central Acts is prepared by the Official Language Wing (Rajbhasha Khand) of the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice.

q: An instructor in a Hindi workshop is asked which institution prepared the standard form of the Devanagari script and of Hindi spelling (Manak Vartani) adopted for official use. The correct answer is:

options.C: The Sahitya Akademi
options.D: The Railway Board

e: The standard form of the Devanagari script and of Hindi spelling, Manak Vartani, for official use was prepared by the Central Hindi Directorate.

q: A school-education note has to record the three languages to be studied in the non-Hindi speaking States under the three-language formula. The correct set is:

options.B: The regional language, English and Urdu
options.C: Hindi, the regional language and French
options.D: The regional language, Hindi and English

e: Under the three-language formula, schools in non-Hindi speaking States study the regional language, Hindi and English.
